source_spans.locator: Psychological Review 108(3), published pp.624-625, Abstract and 'The Conflict Monitoring Hypothesis': proposed evaluative mechanism, conflict-to-control feedback, and the distinction between monitoring/evaluation and regulative control

Psychological Review 108(3), published pp.630-631, Simulation Study 1 General Methods / Implementing conflict monitoring: conflict operationalized as simultaneous activation of incompatible representations and quantified with a conflict-monitoring unit using response-layer energy

Psychological Review 108(3), published pp.638-639, Part 2 / Simulation Study 2 General Methods: trial-wise control varies as a function of conflict on preceding trials; integrated conflict drives subsequent control with an exponentially weighted history

Psychological Review 108(3), published pp.643-644, Simulation Study 2 General Discussion and Questions for Future Investigation: closed-loop simulations account for strategic behavioral adjustments; ACC-to-control causal interpretation is proposed but existing support is explicitly described as indirect

Psychological Review 108(3), published pp.644-646, future-investigation discussion: conflict measurement is not uniquely fixed by Hopfield energy and the information content conveyed from monitoring to control remains unresolved

conditions: connectionist task models in which incompatible response representations can be coactive and a separate top-down control input can bias processing
population: human conflict-task performance phenomena modeled in Stroop, Eriksen flanker, and simple forced-choice paradigms
substrate: connectionist response/output units plus separate context or regulatory units
a medial frontal monitoring region proposed as a neural implementation; its causal influence on downstream regulation is treated by the source as not yet directly established
task: computational simulation of conflict-related activation and trial-to-trial behavioral adjustment in Stroop, Eriksen flanker, and simple forced-choice tasks
temporal_scope: within a trial, conflict is computed across processing cycles; conflict accumulated over preceding trials contributes to the control signal applied on subsequent trials through an exponentially weighted history

nodes.description: simultaneous activation of incompatible representations, operationalized in the modeled tasks primarily as coactivation of mutually inhibiting response units
source-proposed monitoring mechanism, implemented in the simulations as a dedicated unit that evaluates the current amount of representational competition
scalar conflict quantity computed from coactivation of incompatible units; Hopfield energy is the simulation measure but is explicitly not claimed to be the unique biological algorithm
integrated conflict from preceding trials, retained as an exponentially weighted history used to update the current control signal
separate context or control units whose activity biases task processing and whose strength is varied in the closed-loop simulations
trial-to-trial strengthening or weakening of top-down control produced from preceding conflict values in Simulation Study 2
modeled reaction-time, accuracy, interference, and related strategic behavioral effects following changes in top-down control
computational simulations used to test whether the proposed monitoring and feedback mechanisms are sufficient to reproduce the targeted activation patterns and behavioral adjustment phenomena

relations.description: the monitoring mechanism maps coactivation of incompatible representations to a scalar conflict signal in the computational implementation
conflict accumulated on each trial contributes to the weighted history of preceding conflict used by the feedback model
within Simulation Study 2, higher preceding conflict strengthens top-down control and lower preceding conflict weakens it
conflict measured on preceding trial(s) temporally precedes and contributes to the control setting applied on a subsequent trial
in the closed-loop computational models, changes in top-down control alter subsequent modeled reaction time, accuracy, interference, or related strategic behavior
the simulation studies evaluate whether the proposed monitoring and feedback architecture is sufficient to reproduce the targeted behavioral and activation patterns
